# Design Tokens & the Chakra Theme Layer — Knowledge Base

Extracted from the SFCC-55 global-footer session (18–21 Aug 2026), then **re-verified against the
live repo on 2026-08-22** (`feature/SFCC-55_global-footer-ui` @ `ec9d161`). Every quantitative claim
below was re-measured today unless explicitly marked otherwise.

Scope: the token derivation chain, Chakra scale registration, `extendTheme` semantics, `textStyle`
expansion, provisional-token governance, token mirrors, units policy, `globalStyles.ts`.

---

## 0. The architecture in one diagram

```
foundation/colour.ts  ─┐
foundation/typography.ts│  primitive consts, then a semantic/alias tier
foundation/spacing.ts   │  that REFERENCES the primitives (never retypes)
foundation/sizes.ts     ├─→ foundation/zimmTokens.ts   (fully DERIVED; imports from all of the above)
foundation/gridSystem.ts│         │
foundation/motion.ts   ─┘         │
                                  ├─→ theme/zimmTokensGlobal.tsx  → raw Emotion <Global> → :root { --zimm-* }
                                  │      mounted TWICE: _app-config/index.tsx AND .storybook/preview.tsx
                                  │
foundation/index.ts ──→ theme/index.ts ── extendTheme(baseTheme, overrides) ──→ ChakraProvider
                             │                                                        │
                             ├─ registers: borderWidths, breakpoints, colors,         └─ toCSSVar()
                             │             fonts, space, textStyles, components,          populates __cssMap
                             │             styles.global
                             │
                             └─ theme/components/*.ts  (recipes; consume var(--zimm-*) + registered keys)
                                        │
                                        └─→ component JSX via __css={styles.part} / useMultiStyleConfig
```

**Direction is one-way and load-bearing.** `zimmTokens.ts` imports *from* `typography.ts` et al.
Therefore `typography.ts` **physically cannot** write `fontSize: 'var(--zimm-font-size-4xs)'` — that
is a circular import. The CSS-var registry is *downstream* of the values, a delivery mechanism, not
the source of truth. Verified live: `zimmTokens.ts:6-12` imports from `fonts`, `colour`, `typography`,
`spacing`, `sizes`, `gridSystem`, `motion`.

---

# (a) RULES

Imperative and testable. Each has its enforcement mechanism noted — several have **none**, which is
itself the finding.

### R1. Set type with `textStyle`, never a raw `fontSize`/`lineHeight`/`letterSpacing` token key.
All 22 Handover text styles are registered (verified: `Object.keys(theme.textStyles).length === 22`).
`fontSizes`, `lineHeights`, `letterSpacings` are **deliberately NOT registered as Chakra scales**.
Enforcement: `recipeGuards.test.ts` guard 2 — but **only inside registered recipes**, not JSX props.

### R2. Never put a bare named-scale key on a sizing prop.
`width`/`height`/`boxSize`/`min|maxWidth|Height` (+ `w`/`h`/`minW`/… aliases) resolve through
**`theme.sizes`**. Only `theme.space` carries the Zimmermann named scale. Use
`var(--zimm-scale-<name>)`, an imported `foundation/` constant, or an explicit unit.
Enforcement: `recipeGuards.test.ts` guard 1 (recipes only).

### R3. Spacing props (`padding`/`margin`/`gap`/`inset`/`top`…) SHOULD use the bare named key.
`padding: 'xs'` → `var(--chakra-space-xs)`. This is the prescribed form (`overrideStyling.md`
"Component-local tokens"). R2 and R3 are opposite rules for the same key strings — that asymmetry is
the single most dangerous thing in this codebase's styling layer.

### R4. Never put a scale key inside a compound (multi-value) shorthand.
Chakra resolves a token only when it is the **entire** value. Use axis props (`paddingY`/`paddingX`)
or make every component a `var()`. Enforcement: `recipeGuards.test.ts` guard 4.

### R5. Namespace every new recipe key with a `Zimm` prefix unless the merge is intended.
`extendTheme` **deep-merges**. SFCC ships a `Footer` recipe (verified: `theme.components.Footer`
exists in the base). The only intentional merges today are `Button`, `Header`, `ListMenu` — these are
an explicit allowlist in `recipeGuards.test.ts` guard 5. Everything else: `ZimmFooter`, `ZimmNavItem`,
`ZimmTextInput`.

### R6. If a merge IS intended, never introduce a CSS **shorthand** on a part where the base sets a **longhand**.
Merge key-ordering rule: a key that already exists in the base is overwritten **in place** (keeps the
base's position); a key you add that the base lacks is appended **last**. So your `margin: 0` lands
after the base's `marginBottom` and wipes it. (Verbatim from the session's own doc line:
*"never introduce a CSS shorthand on a part where the base sets longhands, because your new key is
appended last and wins."*)

### R7. Never edit `zimmTokens.ts` to add a value. Edit the owning `foundation/*.ts` file.
`zimmTokens.ts` is derived. A hand-typed entry there becomes a second copy of a value. Note both are
Tier 1, so either way it is a UI-designer escalation.

### R8. Never consume a numeric alias — `var(--zimm-scale-NNN)`.
`--zimm-scale-1200` says nothing about intent; `--zimm-scale-xl` does. The numeric aliases are
Handover ports that exist "for completeness, not consumption". **Live violations today (5, all
pre-dating SFCC-55):** `theme/components/listMenu.ts:17,33,65,84` (`--zimm-scale-700`) and
`theme/components/header.ts:59` (`--zimm-scale-1200`). Enforcement: **none**. Not covered by
`recipeGuards.test.ts`, not covered by any ast-grep rule.

### R9. The alias tier references the primitive tier — it never retypes a value.
`colour.ts` defines `grey`/`ivory`/… as plain consts first, then `text.default: grey[900]`. Do the
same for any new primitive/alias pair. Verified live at `colour.ts:1-108`.

### R10. Units: `rem` to scale, `px` for hairline, `em` for breakpoints only.
- **`rem`** — type (`fontSize`/`lineHeight`/`letterSpacing`) and all spacing. WCAG 1.4.4: must
  survive browser zoom / user root font-size.
- **`px`** — border widths, focus-ring offsets, and (provisionally) `button.ts`'s heights.
- **`em`** — `gridSystem.ts` breakpoints, deliberately, so media queries shift with zoom. Also
  `footer.ts`'s `BP` block: *"media queries cannot consume `var()`"* — the one sanctioned reason a
  `theme/components/*.ts` file imports `foundation/` directly.
- Verified safe: neither the Zimmermann theme nor the base SFCC theme sets a root font-size, so the
  original px→rem conversion was a clean 1:1.

### R11. A value being a literal in the emitted CSS is NOT a defect. The invariant is single-sourcing.
The real test is **"is this value typed more than once?"** — not "does it use `var()`". Session's own
worked examples:
- ✅ `font-size: 0.625rem` — typed once, in `typography.ts` as `fontSizes['4xs']`.
- ✅ `width: 16px` — typed once, in `sizes.ts` as `iconSizes.md`.
- ❌ a hand-typed `const X = '3rem'` sitting beside an existing token holding 3rem — two copies, free
  to drift.

### R12. One canonical styling surface per interactive component: its `theme/components/<name>.ts`.
Do not also give it a `.zimm-*` global class. A static class cannot express
`_hover`/`_active`/`_disabled`/`_focusVisible`, so a class "mirror" is structurally incomplete from
birth. Verified: `globalStyles.ts` contains **zero** `.zimm-btn-*` classes — the only two `zimm-btn`
string hits in the file are comments at lines 93 and 96 recording their deliberate absence.
Correspondingly, `typography.ts` gives `button`/`buttonSm` no `.zimm-text-btn-*` class.

### R13. Inside a recipe, order matters against an expanded `textStyle`.
`sx` outranks the `textStyle` **prop**; `__css` does not. If a recipe needs to override one property
of a `textStyle`, write that property **after** `textStyle:` in the same object and drop the JSX-level
`textStyle`/`sx`. Live precedent — `zimmNavItem.ts`: `textStyle: 'navigation'` followed by
`fontFamily: 'var(--zimm-font-family-body)'` with the comment *"deliberately overrides the spread"*.

### R14. For an SVG `fill`/`stroke` **attribute**, use `useToken`, not a `var()`.
An SVG presentation attribute needs a concrete colour. Live pattern:
`const [inverseColour, defaultColour] = useToken('colors', ['text.inverse', 'text.default'])`.

### R15. `--zimm-*` belongs in the theme layer, never in component JSX.
Component files use rung 1–2 of the hierarchy (`textStyle`, semantic token strings). `var(--zimm-*)`
is a `theme/components/*.ts` and `globalStyles.ts` idiom. This resolved an apparent PR #56-vs-#52
contradiction: they are different layers and both were right.

### R16. `.zimm-*` classes are for static, non-interactive, massively-reused treatments only.
Typography, the responsive grid, form-field layout. **27 classes exist** (verified), of which 20 are
`.zimm-text-*`. **Adoption is still effectively zero:** exactly one consumer repo-wide,
`overrides/app/components/foundation/spacing.stories.tsx:79` (`className="zimm-grid"`).

### R17. Any offline Chakra assertion must wrap the theme in `toCSSVar()` first.
**`extendTheme` does not populate `theme.__cssMap` — only `ChakraProvider` does, via `toCSSVar`.**
Verified live today: `raw theme __cssMap present: false` → `after toCSSVar __cssMap: true`. Without
the wrap, `css({color:'text.default'})(theme)` returns `{"color":"text.default"}` — unresolved — and
even Chakra's own `space` keys fail. Any test or audit script that skips this **passes for the wrong
reason**.

### R18. State the provisional-ness at the point of use, with the Figma alias path.
The sanctioned pattern for a value with no foundation home: a named local `const`, in `rem` where it
should scale, with a comment carrying (a) the Figma alias path it is waiting for, (b) the confirmed
value, (c) who owns the decision. `footer.ts:17-35` and `zimmTextInput.ts:26-37` are the reference
implementations. The Figma alias path (`alias/size/footer/col-width-nav`) is the **foreign key** that
makes a code-side registry joinable to the designer-side spec — write it even before any tooling
consumes it.

---

# (b) TRAPS

Each re-verified today by evaluating the real composed theme through
`css(...)(toCSSVar(theme))`. Raw measured output is quoted.

---

### T1. The space-vs-sizes trap — a bare scale key on a sizing prop

**Symptom.** A 24px icon renders 576px and destroys the page layout. Passes `tsc`, `eslint`,
`vitest`, CodeRabbit and the Storybook a11y run. Only rendering catches it.

**Root cause.** The Zimmermann named scale is registered as **`space` only** (`theme/index.ts:56`,
`space: spacing`). Sizing props resolve through `theme.sizes`, which is still Chakra's default.

**Measured today** (`theme.space` vs `theme.sizes`, px-equivalent):

| key | `space` (intended) | `sizes` (what `width:` gets) | error |
|---|---|---|---|
| `3xs` | 2 | 224 | **112×** |
| `2xs` | 4 | 256 | 64× |
| `xs` | 8 | 320 | 40× |
| `s` | 12 | *(no key)* | **DROPPED** |
| `m` | 16 | *(no key)* | **DROPPED** |
| `l` | 20 | *(no key)* | **DROPPED** |
| `xl` | 24 | 576 | 24× |
| `2xl` | 32 | 672 | 21× |
| `3xl` | 40 | 768 | 19× |
| `4xl` | 64 | 896 | 14× |
| `5xl` | 80 | 1024 | 12.8× |
| `6xl` | 128 | 1152 | 9× |
| `7xl` | 160 | 1280 | 8× |

Note the asymmetry: `s`/`m`/`l` have no Chakra `sizes` key at all, so those silently emit **nothing**
rather than a wrong value. Two different failure modes from the same mistake.

**Fix.** `width: 'var(--zimm-scale-xl)'` (verified: passes through verbatim), or an imported
`foundation/` constant, or an explicit unit.

**Why the scale isn't just registered as `sizes` too:** `theme/index.ts:39` — Chakra's `sizes.lg` is
32rem and backs every `w`/`h`/`boxSize` token across the base retail-react-app; remapping would
resize base components at ~199 call sites.

---

### T2. The same trap on typography props — two distinct failure modes

**Measured today:**

```
fontSize:'2xs'    ->  {"fontSize":"var(--chakra-fontSizes-2xs)"}   // = 0.625rem (10px)
                                                                   // Zimmermann 2xs = 0.875rem (14px)
fontSize:'l'      ->  {"fontSize":"l"}                             // no such key -> browser DROPS
lineHeight:'2xs'  ->  {"lineHeight":"2xs"}                         // no such key -> browser DROPS
```

**Root cause.** `fontSizes`/`lineHeights`/`letterSpacings` are deliberately not registered
(`theme/index.ts:35-36` lists 4 direct collisions where Chakra and Zimmermann use the same key name
for different values). `fontSizes` is the only one of the three with genuine *wrong-value*
collisions; the other two only ever drop.

**LIVE INSTANCE, still shipping:** `overrides/app/components/header/index.tsx:302` —
`<Text as="h2" fontSize="l" ...>`. Verified today: `theme.fontSizes.l === undefined`, so this emits
`font-size: l` and the browser discards it. Pre-dates SFCC-55 (`develop:293`).

**Why nothing catches it:** `recipeGuards.test.ts` walks the *registered recipe map* only. Its own
docstring names this exact instance as out of reach and prescribes the fix — a static rule over JSX
attributes in `.coderabbit/ast-grep-rules/`. **That rule does not exist.** The directory holds only
three a11y rules (`img-missing-alt`, `icon-button-missing-aria-label`,
`clickable-non-interactive-element`); grepping `.coderabbit/` for `fontSize|hex|token` returns nothing.

---

### T3. The compound-shorthand trap

**Symptom.** A padding or margin simply does not apply. No error anywhere.

**Measured today:**

```
padding:'xs'          ->  {"padding":"var(--chakra-space-xs)"}                        // OK
padding:'xs 0'        ->  {"padding":"xs 0"}                                          // emitted VERBATIM
paddingY:'xs',X:0     ->  {"paddingTop":"var(--chakra-space-xs)", ...}                // FIX
```

**Root cause.** Chakra resolves a token only as the *entire* value. `"xs 0"` is not a token, so it
passes through, and `padding: xs 0` is invalid CSS — the browser drops the whole declaration.

**Fix.** Axis props, or make every component a `var()`. Note: a compound that is *fully* `var()`-based
is valid — `footer.ts:447,458,468` (`gap: '0 var(--zimm-scale-2xl)'`) were audited and passed.

Four instances of this shipped on the footer branch before the guard existed.

---

### T4. The `extendTheme` merge collision

**Symptom.** Two independent, unrelated-looking visual bugs: footer copyright rendered **14px instead
of 10px**, and the subscribe heading lost its **24px** bottom gap (rendered 0). Plus a mystery
`padding-top` at a breakpoint (`min-width: 62em`) the project doesn't even use.

**Root cause.** `theme/index.ts:64` is `extendTheme(baseTheme, overrides)` — a **deep merge**. SFCC
ships its own `Footer` multipart recipe (verified: `theme.components.Footer` exists in the base).
Naming ours `Footer` merged into it rather than replacing it. 4 of 33 part names collided:
`container`, `subscribe`, `subscribeHeading`, `copyright`.

- Base `copyright: {fontSize:'sm', marginBottom:6, color:'gray.50'}` → base's literal `fontSize:'sm'`
  (14px) beat our `textStyle:'footer'` (10px), and imported a stray 24px bottom margin.
- Base `subscribeHeading` already had `marginBottom: 2`. Our value overwrote it **in place** at
  position 3; our *new* `margin: 0` key was appended **last** and the shorthand reset it → 0px gap.

Critically: **in isolation Chakra emitted the correct order.** The reordering only happens because of
the merge, which is why unit-testing the recipe alone would not have caught it.

**Fix.** Rename to `ZimmFooter`. Verified fixed: copyright 14px→10px, stray margin gone,
`subscribeHeading` gap 0→24px.

**Historical footnote worth keeping:** the older prototype looked *closer* to Figma because it used
inline `style` attributes, which bypass the theme entirely. Migrating to the recipe was the correct
architectural move (`overrideStyling.md` mandates it) — it just walked into a collision nobody knew
about. Do not read "the inline version looked right" as evidence against recipes.

---

### T5. `textStyle` expands to literals — this is correct, not a token violation

**Symptom (of the *audit*, not the code).** A CSS-provenance sweep reports ~36 occurrences / 14
distinct "raw literal" declarations in the footer's emitted CSS. It looks like a large token-hygiene
failure. **~85% of it is `textStyle` working exactly as designed.**

**Measured today:**

```
textStyle:'footer' -> {"fontFamily":"'Futura Round', ...","fontSize":"0.625rem","fontWeight":"500",
                       "lineHeight":"0.875rem","letterSpacing":"0.025rem","textTransform":"uppercase"}
```

Six resolved literals, zero `var()`.

**Root cause.** Chakra walks `theme.textStyles.footer` → `fontSizes['4xs']` → `'0.625rem'` and emits
it. The var was never in that path — and *cannot* be, because `zimmTokens.ts` imports from
`typography.ts`, so making `typography.ts` emit `var(--zimm-font-size-4xs)` would be a circular
import and would promote the CSS-var mirror to source of truth.

**The three emission paths — know which one you're looking at before calling something a defect:**

| You write | You get | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `zIndex:'overlay'`, `padding:'xs'` | `var(--chakra-*)` | Chakra recognises a registered scale key |
| `width:'var(--zimm-scale-xl)'` | `var(--zimm-*)` | opaque string, passed through verbatim |
| `textStyle:'footer'` | **resolved literal** | composite, expanded at build time |

**Consequence for auditing.** A "raw literal in emitted CSS" bucket is not a defect count. Its only
valid use is as a cross-check: anything in it that *isn't* explained by theme expansion is a
hand-typed duplicate. The source-level mirror check is what actually pins those down.

---

### T6. The token-mirror false positive — value equality is not token equality

**This is the most important self-correction in the whole session.** At 10:43 the session declared
two hand-typed constants actionable and proposed the diff. At 10:46 it retracted: *"Don't fix these —
I was wrong to call them actionable."*

The two constants:

```ts
const SPACE_SECTION = '3rem';    // alias/space/section (48px)
const SIZE_COL_NAV  = '8.75rem'; // alias/size/footer/col-width-nav (140px)
```

The "obvious" fix — point them at `var(--zimm-scale-1200)` (48px) and `var(--zimm-scale-3500)`
(140px) — breaks three ways:

1. **WCAG 1.4.4 regression.** Those aliases are authored in **px**. `3rem` scales with browser zoom;
   `48px` does not. The current code is *more correct* than the replacement.
2. **Violates R8** (numeric-alias consumption). Would introduce two fresh violations into a check
   that was at zero for this file.
3. **No legitimate token to point at.** Verified programmatically: the named scale jumps
   `3xl` = 2.5rem → `4xl` = 4rem, straight past 3rem; and `6xl` = 8rem → `7xl` = 10rem, past
   8.75rem. Confirmed again today against the live `spacing.ts`.

A third flagged "mirror" — `SIZE_MODAL_SUB = '30rem'` ≡ `breakpoints.sm = '30em'` — is a pure
**coincidental value collision**. A modal max-width has no semantic relationship to a breakpoint.

**So all three "style mirrors" the automated check reported were false positives.** The check matches
on normalised value alone and is blind to: unit semantics, semantic role, and whether the token it
matched is one you are even permitted to use.

**Rule this yields:** before "fixing" a mirror, check three gates — same unit, same semantic scale,
and target is a permitted (non-numeric-alias) token. If any fails, the local constant is correct and
**the gap is upstream** — the foundation needs a new named entry, which is Tier 1 / designer work.

The live code now documents exactly this at `footer.ts:20-24`, citing WCAG 1.4.4.

---

### T7. The `z-index` guess that was never a token gap

`MODAL_Z_INDEX = 1000` looked like a provisional design value. It was a live Sev3-class defect.
Chakra already ships `dropdown:1000 · sticky:1100 · banner:1200 · overlay:1300 · modal:1400 ·
toast:1700`. `header.ts` sets `zIndex:'sticky'` (1100); the footer's portalled modal overlay was
1000 — so the sticky header painted **above** the dimmed backdrop, visible, clickable, and focusable.
`1000` being *exactly* Chakra's `dropdown` was the tell that it was picked by guess.

Fixed and verified live: `footer.ts:177` is now `zIndex: 'overlay'`.

**Rule:** before classifying a numeric literal as a designer dependency, check whether the framework
already ships a semantic token for it.

---

### T8. Vacuous audit passes (the meta-trap)

Three distinct instances in one session, all in the token/theme audit tooling:

- **`css()` without `toCSSVar`** (R17) — every token silently unresolved; assertions pass for the
  wrong reason.
- **A guard that asserts an empty offender list** passes just as happily on empty *input*. Fixed by
  adding an explicit non-vacuity test — live at `recipeGuards.test.ts`:
  `test('collect() actually walks the registered recipes')`, asserting `components` and `collect()`
  are both non-empty. *"Without this, deleting `components` would turn the whole file green."*
- **A hand-curated file list instead of a directory walk.** Phase 1 used 13 files; `overrides/` has
  71; **7 of the 20 files the PR changed were outside the list** — which is precisely why an inline
  style in `header/index.tsx` never appeared in the reported count.

Related regex-level false results the session had to retract: a `var()` extraction regex missing the
`i` flag truncated `--chakra-lineHeights-normal` at the uppercase `H` and reported 4 phantom
"undefined var" findings; and a `zimm-scale-[0-9]` regex matches the leading digit of `3xs`/`2xl`,
inflating the numeric-alias count from 5 to 24. **Use `var\(--zimm-scale-[0-9]+\)`.**

---

# (c) METHODS — how to actually audit this

### M1. Offline recipe/theme probe (the highest-value tool in the session)

Bundle the theme with esbuild and evaluate it through Chakra's own resolver. This is how every trap
above was *proved* rather than asserted.

```bash
# 1. Bundle (works for foundation/index.ts, theme/index.ts, or a single recipe)
npx esbuild overrides/app/theme/index.ts --bundle --format=cjs --platform=node \
  --outfile=/tmp/theme.cjs --log-level=error --external:react --external:react-dom

# 2. Evaluate — NOTE the toCSSVar wrap; without it every result is garbage (R17)
node -e '
const P="./node_modules/";
const {css, toCSSVar} = require(P+"@chakra-ui/styled-system");
const t = toCSSVar(require("/tmp/theme.cjs").default);
const run = (o) => JSON.stringify(css(o)(t));
console.log("compound :", run({padding:"xs 0"}));      // -> "xs 0"  (BAD)
console.log("sizing   :", run({width:"xl"}));          // -> var(--chakra-sizes-xl) = 36rem (BAD)
console.log("typo     :", run({fontSize:"l"}));        // -> "l"     (DROPPED)
console.log("textStyle:", run({textStyle:"footer"}));  // -> 6 resolved literals (CORRECT)
'
```

Use it for: proving a trap exists, proving a fix is byte-identical to what it replaces (the session
proved a `textStyles.serif` substitution identical across all 9 properties in both `inverse` modes
this way), and confirming that a shared base const isn't mutated by the `extendTheme` merge.

### M2. Mechanical guards — `overrides/app/theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts`

**5 tests, all passing** (verified today: `npx vitest run overrides/app/theme` → 150/150 across 4
files). Four guards + one non-vacuity meta-test:

| Guard | Catches |
|---|---|
| 1 | bare spacing-scale key on a sizing prop (T1) |
| 2 | bare scale key on `fontSize`/`lineHeight`/`letterSpacing` (T2) |
| 3 | bare scale key inside a compound shorthand (T4/T3) |
| 4 | recipe key colliding with a base SFCC recipe (T4), allowlist `['Button','Header','ListMenu']` |
| — | `collect()` actually walks a non-empty recipe map (T8) |

Two design details worth preserving if this is ever extended:
- **Guard 4 asserts on the recipe *name*, not on diffed keys.** An earlier version diffed top-level
  `baseStyle` keys, which would pass while the base injected properties nested inside a part, or via
  `variants`/`sizes`. The name is what actually determines whether `extendTheme` merges — deterministic,
  not inferred. (CodeRabbit was right about this.)
- **`isResponsiveContainer` must test "are ALL keys breakpoints?", never "is ANY key?"** `xl`/`2xl`
  are keys in both `breakpoints` and `spacing`; `sm`/`md`/`lg` are keys in both `breakpoints` and
  `fontSizes`. A per-key test cannot distinguish a responsive map from a style object.
- **`fontWeight` is deliberately absent** from the typography guard: `medium` is a key in both scales
  and resolves to 500 either way, so guarding it would flag correct code.

**Known scope limit (documented in the file's own docstring):** these walk the registered recipe map
only. They cannot see the same mistake made as a JSX prop. See T2's live instance.

### M3. Theme-registration collision guards — `overrides/app/theme/index.test.tsx`

125 tests. The ones that matter for token governance are the **negative** assertions — they exist to
fail loudly if someone "helpfully" registers a scale:

- `fontSizes are NOT remapped to the Zimmermann scale`
- `transition durations are NOT remapped to the Zimmermann motion scale`
- `sizes are NOT remapped to the Zimmermann icon or action scales`
- `every textStyle has a matching .zimm-text-* class, except the documented exceptions`
- `the colour palette is fully mapped`
- `the font families are a single shared definition, not a copy`
- `extendTheme merges rather than replaces the base colour scales`

Treat a failure here as a real drift signal, not test noise. This file renders through a real
provider, so it is unaffected by the `__cssMap` trap.

### M4. Source-level sweeps (regex; know the limits)

```bash
# Numeric-alias consumption (R8). Note the trailing + and ) — a bare [0-9] matches "3xs".
grep -rnE 'var\(--zimm-scale-[0-9]+\)' overrides/ --include='*.ts' --include='*.tsx' \
  | grep -v 'foundation/zimmTokens'
# -> 5 hits today: listMenu.ts:17,33,65,84 ; header.ts:59

# Compound space values in recipes (T3)
grep -rnE "(padding|margin|inset|gap)[A-Za-z]*: *'[^']* [^']*'" overrides/app/theme/components/*.ts \
  | grep -v '\.test\.'

# Raw fontSize props in JSX (T2 — the class recipeGuards cannot reach)
grep -rn 'fontSize=' overrides/app/components/ --include='*.tsx'
```

**Stated limits, from the session's own caveat list:** regex is blind to computed values, template
literals built from variables, styles assembled at runtime, and values passed down as props. Prefer a
**walk over changed files**, never a hand-curated list (T8).

### M5. The provisional-token inventory method (this is the reusable process)

The audit that turned "we're blocked on the designer" into an actionable 29-item inventory:

1. Bundle `foundation/index.ts` to CJS with esbuild and **load it at runtime** — so token values are
   real evaluated values, not regex guesses. (Yielded 76 distinct normalised values across `colors`,
   `spacing`, `typography`, `sizes`, `gridSystem`, `motion` + all `zimmTokens` entries.)
2. Normalise every literal to a common basis: lengths → px-equivalent (`rem`/`em` × 16), colours →
   canonical `rgba()`, durations → ms. So `3rem`, `48px` and `--zimm-scale-1200` compare as one value.
3. **Gate matches on semantic-scale compatibility** — otherwise a modal width matching a breakpoint
   reports as a hit (T6/C-3).
4. Compute scope split with `git grep` against `origin/develop` per constant, so inherited debt isn't
   attributed to the current PR.

**The classification buckets — reuse these verbatim; they are the product:**

| Bucket | Meaning | Local token appropriate? | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A** | Already has an official token | ❌ delete the provisional | FED |
| **B** | **Conflicts** with an official token | ❌ needs a decision | UI Designer |
| **C** | Duplicate of another provisional | ❌ plain DRY fix | FED |
| **D1** | Missing token, **value confirmed** | ✅ **the only valid target** | UI Designer |
| **D2** | Missing token, **value guessed** | ❌ "a guess in token clothing" | UI Designer (spec first) |
| **E** | Not a design gap at all | ❌ framework token exists | FED — often a **live defect** |

**Headline result: only 7 of 29 were true "missing token, value confirmed".** The rest were 5
duplicates, 4 conflicts, 1 DRY pair, ~8 guesses, and 1 framework token that already existed (T7).
An initial estimate of ~60% D1 fell to ~25% once measured.

**Bucket-B rule, stated as a principle:** *"A local token here enshrines a value already known to be
contested, closes the story on a wrong pixel, and surfaces the defect later, further from its cause."*
Never launder a Category B value into "closed" — if a story ships on a contested value, the AC must
say so.

---

# (d) OPEN QUESTIONS / UNRATIFIED DECISIONS

1. **`scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs` does not exist.** `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md:32` instructs
   developers to run it before any PR touching `overrides/app/components/**` or
   `overrides/app/theme/components/**`. **Verified missing today** (`scripts/` contains 13 entries,
   none of them this). The session's own assessment: *"That is a large part of why 29 literals
   accumulated unnoticed."* Also not wired to CI, and `overrideStyling.md` already anticipates why
   (false positives on hairline px need a human triager).

2. **The `@local-token` system was designed and explicitly NOT built.** Verbatim, 15:57 on 19 Aug:
   *"no local-token implementation in this PR. The 8 remaining provisionals in `footer.ts` stay
   exactly as they are: plain `const`s with prose comments. No `@local-token` markers, no generated
   registry, no `auditTokenUsage.mjs`, no CSS-var shadow pattern."* Four planned pieces:
   structured `@local-token` JSDoc marker (`figma:`/`value:`/`owner:`/`raised:`/`category:`);
   `.claude/registry/tokens.md` generated by extending the existing `scripts/generateRegistry.mjs`;
   `auditTokenUsage.mjs`; and a join to Han Lee's f2r specs via the Figma alias path.

3. **BLOCKED ON TIM: may a Tier 2 file *declare* a `--zimm-*` custom property?** No file does today.
   The proposal was to declare a local on the component root
   (`root: {'--zimm-size-field-height': '36px'}`) so consumers read the final name and closing the
   local is a one-line delete. **The risk that blocks it:** a component-scoped custom property
   *overrides* the inherited `:root` value, so a local left behind after the real token lands would
   **silently shadow it** — the component keeps the placeholder while the rest of the app moves on.
   Strictly worse than today's failure mode, and invisible. Safe only alongside a mechanical
   leftover check — i.e. `auditTokenUsage.mjs` is a **prerequisite, not a follow-up**.

4. **BLOCKED ON DELIVERY: does a Category B (contested-value) token block the story, or ship with a
   declared deviation?** Named as the question that decides whether the whole system speeds the team
   up or merely documents the slowdown.

5. **The named scale is `rem`; the numeric Handover aliases are `px` — same conceptual scale, same
   file, two units.** Flagged for the designer (Kiera). This inconsistency is what made T6 look like
   a fix in the first place, and *"it'll mislead the next person too."*

6. **DOC DRIFT — `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md:65` is wrong and was never corrected.** It claims
   the 7 numeric aliases with no named-scale equivalent are *"not duplicates, just Handover values
   with nothing to derive them from."* Two of them (`1200` = 48px, `3500` = 140px) now have exact
   value twins in `footer.ts` (`SPACE_SECTION`, `SIZE_COL_NAV`) — differing only in unit. Tier 1
   governance, so it was raised as a flag rather than edited. **Still uncorrected today.**

7. **DOC DRIFT — `theme/index.ts:47-49` says "The 15 numeric `--zimm-scale-NNN` aliases are
   duplicates of the named scale."** Verified: there are 15 numeric aliases, but only **8** are
   derived from the named scale; **7** are standalone literals (`025`, `700`, `1100`, `1200`, `1300`,
   `3500`, `4500`). The blanket "are duplicates" is imprecise in the opposite direction to item 6.
   Minor, but the two Tier 1 docs now disagree with each other about the same 15 values.

8. **Unresolved Bucket-B conflicts still live in the code:**
   - `button.ts:205-207` — `BTN_HEIGHT_LG='50px'` vs `actionSizes.height.lg='52px'` (−2px);
     `BTN_HEIGHT_SM='41px'` vs `actionSizes.height.md='40px'` (+1px); `BTN_PADDING_Y='5px'` with no
     Handover token at all. All three still present, still flagged in-file.
   - `navConstants.ts` — `NAV_LETTER_SPACING = 0.02em` vs `textStyles.navigation` → `letterSpacings.sm
     = '0'`. Also breaches the units rule (`em` outside breakpoints).
   - `footer.ts:14` — `BP.desktop = '64em'` (1024px) maps to **no** Chakra breakpoint (`lg`=62em,
     `xl`=80em). **Highest-impact of the four:** it is why every desktop rule in `footer.ts` is a raw
     `@media` and unreachable via Chakra responsive props. Should be decided first.
   - `button.ts:17` — `ICON_TRANSITION = 'opacity 0.15s ease'`, a raw duration not sourced from
     `motion.ts` (which is itself marked PROVISIONAL), deliberately left rather than retimed silently.

9. **`motion.ts` is wholly PROVISIONAL** ("Motion design is pending formal sign-off… Do not treat as
   final"), yet its values are already published as six `--zimm-motion-*` vars and consumed by
   `zimmTextInput.ts`. Not wrong, but it means motion sign-off will be a multi-file change.

10. **`globalStyles.ts` ships on every page regardless of use.** Registered as one
    `theme.styles.global` block. Per-component CSS loading is logged as a separate, unscoped
    initiative. Given adoption is one Storybook demo (R16), the whole registry is currently
    near-pure overhead.

11. **`FONT_SERIF` has no `@font-face`.** `textStyles.serif` resolves to Georgia today. Self-host
    Source Serif 4 when a component first needs it.

---

# (e) COULD NOT VERIFY

- **The 6 additional numeric-alias violations in `pdpProductInfo/index.tsx` and

# Design Tokens & the Chakra Theme Layer — Knowledge Base

Extracted from the SFCC-55 global-footer session (18–21 Aug 2026), then **re-verified against the
live repo on 2026-08-22** (`feature/SFCC-55_global-footer-ui` @ `ec9d161`). Every quantitative claim
below was re-measured today unless explicitly marked otherwise.

Scope: the token derivation chain, Chakra scale registration, `extendTheme` semantics, `textStyle`
expansion, provisional-token governance, token mirrors, units policy, `globalStyles.ts`.

---

## 0. The architecture in one diagram

```
foundation/colour.ts  ─┐
foundation/typography.ts│  primitive consts, then a semantic/alias tier
foundation/spacing.ts   │  that REFERENCES the primitives (never retypes)
foundation/sizes.ts     ├─→ foundation/zimmTokens.ts   (fully DERIVED; imports from all of the above)
foundation/gridSystem.ts│         │
foundation/motion.ts   ─┘         │
                                  ├─→ theme/zimmTokensGlobal.tsx  → raw Emotion <Global> → :root { --zimm-* }
                                  │      mounted TWICE: _app-config/index.tsx AND .storybook/preview.tsx
                                  │
foundation/index.ts ──→ theme/index.ts ── extendTheme(baseTheme, overrides) ──→ ChakraProvider
                             │                                                        │
                             ├─ registers: borderWidths, breakpoints, colors,         └─ toCSSVar()
                             │             fonts, space, textStyles, components,          populates __cssMap
                             │             styles.global
                             │
                             └─ theme/components/*.ts  (recipes; consume var(--zimm-*) + registered keys)
                                        │
                                        └─→ component JSX via __css={styles.part} / useMultiStyleConfig
```

**Direction is one-way and load-bearing.** `zimmTokens.ts` imports *from* `typography.ts` et al.
Therefore `typography.ts` **physically cannot** write `fontSize: 'var(--zimm-font-size-4xs)'` — that
is a circular import. The CSS-var registry is *downstream* of the values, a delivery mechanism, not
the source of truth. Verified live: `zimmTokens.ts:6-12` imports from `fonts`, `colour`, `typography`,
`spacing`, `sizes`, `gridSystem`, `motion`.

---

# (a) RULES

Imperative and testable. Each has its enforcement mechanism noted — several have **none**, which is
itself the finding.

### R1. Set type with `textStyle`, never a raw `fontSize`/`lineHeight`/`letterSpacing` token key.
All 22 Handover text styles are registered (verified: `Object.keys(theme.textStyles).length === 22`).
`fontSizes`, `lineHeights`, `letterSpacings` are **deliberately NOT registered as Chakra scales**.
Enforcement: `recipeGuards.test.ts` guard 2 — but **only inside registered recipes**, not JSX props.

### R2. Never put a bare named-scale key on a sizing prop.
`width`/`height`/`boxSize`/`min|maxWidth|Height` (+ `w`/`h`/`minW`/… aliases) resolve through
**`theme.sizes`**. Only `theme.space` carries the Zimmermann named scale. Use
`var(--zimm-scale-<name>)`, an imported `foundation/` constant, or an explicit unit.
Enforcement: `recipeGuards.test.ts` guard 1 (recipes only).

### R3. Spacing props (`padding`/`margin`/`gap`/`inset`/`top`…) SHOULD use the bare named key.
`padding: 'xs'` → `var(--chakra-space-xs)`. This is the prescribed form (`overrideStyling.md`
"Component-local tokens"). R2 and R3 are opposite rules for the same key strings — that asymmetry is
the single most dangerous thing in this codebase's styling layer.

### R4. Never put a scale key inside a compound (multi-value) shorthand.
Chakra resolves a token only when it is the **entire** value. Use axis props (`paddingY`/`paddingX`)
or make every component a `var()`. Enforcement: `recipeGuards.test.ts` guard 4.

### R5. Namespace every new recipe key with a `Zimm` prefix unless the merge is intended.
`extendTheme` **deep-merges**. SFCC ships a `Footer` recipe (verified: `theme.components.Footer`
exists in the base). The only intentional merges today are `Button`, `Header`, `ListMenu` — these are
an explicit allowlist in `recipeGuards.test.ts` guard 5. Everything else: `ZimmFooter`, `ZimmNavItem`,
`ZimmTextInput`.

### R6. If a merge IS intended, never introduce a CSS **shorthand** on a part where the base sets a **longhand**.
Merge key-ordering rule: a key that already exists in the base is overwritten **in place** (keeps the
base's position); a key you add that the base lacks is appended **last**. So your `margin: 0` lands
after the base's `marginBottom` and wipes it. (Verbatim from the session's own doc line:
*"never introduce a CSS shorthand on a part where the base sets longhands, because your new key is
appended last and wins."*)

### R7. Never edit `zimmTokens.ts` to add a value. Edit the owning `foundation/*.ts` file.
`zimmTokens.ts` is derived. A hand-typed entry there becomes a second copy of a value. Note both are
Tier 1, so either way it is a UI-designer escalation.

### R8. Never consume a numeric alias — `var(--zimm-scale-NNN)`.
`--zimm-scale-1200` says nothing about intent; `--zimm-scale-xl` does. The numeric aliases are
Handover ports that exist "for completeness, not consumption". **Live violations today (5, all
pre-dating SFCC-55):** `theme/components/listMenu.ts:17,33,65,84` (`--zimm-scale-700`) and
`theme/components/header.ts:59` (`--zimm-scale-1200`). Enforcement: **none**. Not covered by
`recipeGuards.test.ts`, not covered by any ast-grep rule.

### R9. The alias tier references the primitive tier — it never retypes a value.
`colour.ts` defines `grey`/`ivory`/… as plain consts first, then `text.default: grey[900]`. Do the
same for any new primitive/alias pair. Verified live at `colour.ts:1-108`.

### R10. Units: `rem` to scale, `px` for hairline, `em` for breakpoints only.
- **`rem`** — type (`fontSize`/`lineHeight`/`letterSpacing`) and all spacing. WCAG 1.4.4: must
  survive browser zoom / user root font-size.
- **`px`** — border widths, focus-ring offsets, and (provisionally) `button.ts`'s heights.
- **`em`** — `gridSystem.ts` breakpoints, deliberately, so media queries shift with zoom. Also
  `footer.ts`'s `BP` block: *"media queries cannot consume `var()`"* — the one sanctioned reason a
  `theme/components/*.ts` file imports `foundation/` directly.
- Verified safe: neither the Zimmermann theme nor the base SFCC theme sets a root font-size, so the
  original px→rem conversion was a clean 1:1.

### R11. A value being a literal in the emitted CSS is NOT a defect. The invariant is single-sourcing.
The real test is **"is this value typed more than once?"** — not "does it use `var()`". Session's own
worked examples:
- ✅ `font-size: 0.625rem` — typed once, in `typography.ts` as `fontSizes['4xs']`.
- ✅ `width: 16px` — typed once, in `sizes.ts` as `iconSizes.md`.
- ❌ a hand-typed `const X = '3rem'` sitting beside an existing token holding 3rem — two copies, free
  to drift.

### R12. One canonical styling surface per interactive component: its `theme/components/<name>.ts`.
Do not also give it a `.zimm-*` global class. A static class cannot express
`_hover`/`_active`/`_disabled`/`_focusVisible`, so a class "mirror" is structurally incomplete from
birth. Verified: `globalStyles.ts` contains **zero** `.zimm-btn-*` classes — the only two `zimm-btn`
string hits in the file are comments at lines 93 and 96 recording their deliberate absence.
Correspondingly, `typography.ts` gives `button`/`buttonSm` no `.zimm-text-btn-*` class.

### R13. Inside a recipe, order matters against an expanded `textStyle`.
`sx` outranks the `textStyle` **prop**; `__css` does not. If a recipe needs to override one property
of a `textStyle`, write that property **after** `textStyle:` in the same object and drop the JSX-level
`textStyle`/`sx`. Live precedent — `zimmNavItem.ts`: `textStyle: 'navigation'` followed by
`fontFamily: 'var(--zimm-font-family-body)'` with the comment *"deliberately overrides the spread"*.

### R14. For an SVG `fill`/`stroke` **attribute**, use `useToken`, not a `var()`.
An SVG presentation attribute needs a concrete colour. Live pattern:
`const [inverseColour, defaultColour] = useToken('colors', ['text.inverse', 'text.default'])`.

### R15. `--zimm-*` belongs in the theme layer, never in component JSX.
Component files use rung 1–2 of the hierarchy (`textStyle`, semantic token strings). `var(--zimm-*)`
is a `theme/components/*.ts` and `globalStyles.ts` idiom. This resolved an apparent PR #56-vs-#52
contradiction: they are different layers and both were right.

### R16. `.zimm-*` classes are for static, non-interactive, massively-reused treatments only.
Typography, the responsive grid, form-field layout. **27 classes exist** (verified), of which 20 are
`.zimm-text-*`. **Adoption is still effectively zero:** exactly one consumer repo-wide,
`overrides/app/components/foundation/spacing.stories.tsx:79` (`className="zimm-grid"`).

### R17. Any offline Chakra assertion must wrap the theme in `toCSSVar()` first.
**`extendTheme` does not populate `theme.__cssMap` — only `ChakraProvider` does, via `toCSSVar`.**
Verified live today: `raw theme __cssMap present: false` → `after toCSSVar __cssMap: true`. Without
the wrap, `css({color:'text.default'})(theme)` returns `{"color":"text.default"}` — unresolved — and
even Chakra's own `space` keys fail. Any test or audit script that skips this **passes for the wrong
reason**.

### R18. State the provisional-ness at the point of use, with the Figma alias path.
The sanctioned pattern for a value with no foundation home: a named local `const`, in `rem` where it
should scale, with a comment carrying (a) the Figma alias path it is waiting for, (b) the confirmed
value, (c) who owns the decision. `footer.ts:17-35` and `zimmTextInput.ts:26-37` are the reference
implementations. The Figma alias path (`alias/size/footer/col-width-nav`) is the **foreign key** that
makes a code-side registry joinable to the designer-side spec — write it even before any tooling
consumes it.

# (b) TRAPS

Each re-verified today by evaluating the real composed theme through
`css(...)(toCSSVar(theme))`. Raw measured output is quoted.

---

### T1. The space-vs-sizes trap — a bare scale key on a sizing prop

**Symptom.** A 24px icon renders 576px and destroys the page layout. Passes `tsc`, `eslint`,
`vitest`, CodeRabbit and the Storybook a11y run. Only rendering catches it.

**Root cause.** The Zimmermann named scale is registered as **`space` only** (`theme/index.ts:56`,
`space: spacing`). Sizing props resolve through `theme.sizes`, which is still Chakra's default.

**Measured today** (`theme.space` vs `theme.sizes`, px-equivalent):

| key | `space` (intended) | `sizes` (what `width:` gets) | error |
|---|---|---|---|
| `3xs` | 2 | 224 | **112×** |
| `2xs` | 4 | 256 | 64× |
| `xs` | 8 | 320 | 40× |
| `s` | 12 | *(no key)* | **DROPPED** |
| `m` | 16 | *(no key)* | **DROPPED** |
| `l` | 20 | *(no key)* | **DROPPED** |
| `xl` | 24 | 576 | 24× |
| `2xl` | 32 | 672 | 21× |
| `3xl` | 40 | 768 | 19× |
| `4xl` | 64 | 896 | 14× |
| `5xl` | 80 | 1024 | 12.8× |
| `6xl` | 128 | 1152 | 9× |
| `7xl` | 160 | 1280 | 8× |

Note the asymmetry: `s`/`m`/`l` have no Chakra `sizes` key at all, so those silently emit **nothing**
rather than a wrong value. Two different failure modes from the same mistake.

**Fix.** `width: 'var(--zimm-scale-xl)'` (verified: passes through verbatim), or an imported
`foundation/` constant, or an explicit unit.

**Why the scale isn't just registered as `sizes` too:** `theme/index.ts:39` — Chakra's `sizes.lg` is
32rem and backs every `w`/`h`/`boxSize` token across the base retail-react-app; remapping would
resize base components at ~199 call sites.

### T2. The same trap on typography props — two distinct failure modes

**Measured today:**

```
fontSize:'2xs'    ->  {"fontSize":"var(--chakra-fontSizes-2xs)"}   // = 0.625rem (10px)
                                                                   // Zimmermann 2xs = 0.875rem (14px)
fontSize:'l'      ->  {"fontSize":"l"}                             // no such key -> browser DROPS
lineHeight:'2xs'  ->  {"lineHeight":"2xs"}                         // no such key -> browser DROPS
```

**Root cause.** `fontSizes`/`lineHeights`/`letterSpacings` are deliberately not registered
(`theme/index.ts:35-36` lists 4 direct collisions where Chakra and Zimmermann use the same key name
for different values). `fontSizes` is the only one of the three with genuine *wrong-value*
collisions; the other two only ever drop.

**LIVE INSTANCE, still shipping:** `overrides/app/components/header/index.tsx:302` —
`<Text as="h2" fontSize="l" ...>`. Verified today: `theme.fontSizes.l === undefined`, so this emits
`font-size: l` and the browser discards it. Pre-dates SFCC-55 (`develop:293`).

**Why nothing catches it:** `recipeGuards.test.ts` walks the *registered recipe map* only. Its own
docstring names this exact instance as out of reach and prescribes the fix — a static rule over JSX
attributes in `.coderabbit/ast-grep-rules/`. **That rule does not exist.** The directory holds only
three a11y rules (`img-missing-alt`, `icon-button-missing-aria-label`,
`clickable-non-interactive-element`); grepping `.coderabbit/` for `fontSize|hex|token` returns nothing.

### T3. The compound-shorthand trap

**Symptom.** A padding or margin simply does not apply. No error anywhere.

**Measured today:**

```
padding:'xs'          ->  {"padding":"var(--chakra-space-xs)"}                        // OK
padding:'xs 0'        ->  {"padding":"xs 0"}                                          // emitted VERBATIM
paddingY:'xs',X:0     ->  {"paddingTop":"var(--chakra-space-xs)", ...}                // FIX
```

**Root cause.** Chakra resolves a token only as the *entire* value. `"xs 0"` is not a token, so it
passes through, and `padding: xs 0` is invalid CSS — the browser drops the whole declaration.

**Fix.** Axis props, or make every component a `var()`. Note: a compound that is *fully* `var()`-based
is valid — `footer.ts:447,458,468` (`gap: '0 var(--zimm-scale-2xl)'`) were audited and passed.

Four instances of this shipped on the footer branch before the guard existed.

---

### T4. The `extendTheme` merge collision

**Symptom.** Two independent, unrelated-looking visual bugs: footer copyright rendered **14px instead
of 10px**, and the subscribe heading lost its **24px** bottom gap (rendered 0). Plus a mystery
`padding-top` at a breakpoint (`min-width: 62em`) the project doesn't even use.

**Root cause.** `theme/index.ts:64` is `extendTheme(baseTheme, overrides)` — a **deep merge**. SFCC
ships its own `Footer` multipart recipe (verified: `theme.components.Footer` exists in the base).
Naming ours `Footer` merged into it rather than replacing it. 4 of 33 part names collided:
`container`, `subscribe`, `subscribeHeading`, `copyright`.

- Base `copyright: {fontSize:'sm', marginBottom:6, color:'gray.50'}` → base's literal `fontSize:'sm'`
  (14px) beat our `textStyle:'footer'` (10px), and imported a stray 24px bottom margin.
- Base `subscribeHeading` already had `marginBottom: 2`. Our value overwrote it **in place** at
  position 3; our *new* `margin: 0` key was appended **last** and the shorthand reset it → 0px gap.

Critically: **in isolation Chakra emitted the correct order.** The reordering only happens because of
the merge, which is why unit-testing the recipe alone would not have caught it.

**Fix.** Rename to `ZimmFooter`. Verified fixed: copyright 14px→10px, stray margin gone,
`subscribeHeading` gap 0→24px.

**Historical footnote worth keeping:** the older prototype looked *closer* to Figma because it used
inline `style` attributes, which bypass the theme entirely. Migrating to the recipe was the correct
architectural move (`overrideStyling.md` mandates it) — it just walked into a collision nobody knew
about. Do not read "the inline version looked right" as evidence against recipes.

### T5. `textStyle` expands to literals — this is correct, not a token violation

**Symptom (of the *audit*, not the code).** A CSS-provenance sweep reports ~36 occurrences / 14
distinct "raw literal" declarations in the footer's emitted CSS. It looks like a large token-hygiene
failure. **~85% of it is `textStyle` working exactly as designed.**

**Measured today:**

```
textStyle:'footer' -> {"fontFamily":"'Futura Round', ...","fontSize":"0.625rem","fontWeight":"500",
                       "lineHeight":"0.875rem","letterSpacing":"0.025rem","textTransform":"uppercase"}
```

Six resolved literals, zero `var()`.

**Root cause.** Chakra walks `theme.textStyles.footer` → `fontSizes['4xs']` → `'0.625rem'` and emits
it. The var was never in that path — and *cannot* be, because `zimmTokens.ts` imports from
`typography.ts`, so making `typography.ts` emit `var(--zimm-font-size-4xs)` would be a circular
import and would promote the CSS-var mirror to source of truth.

**The three emission paths — know which one you're looking at before calling something a defect:**

| You write | You get | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `zIndex:'overlay'`, `padding:'xs'` | `var(--chakra-*)` | Chakra recognises a registered scale key |
| `width:'var(--zimm-scale-xl)'` | `var(--zimm-*)` | opaque string, passed through verbatim |
| `textStyle:'footer'` | **resolved literal** | composite, expanded at build time |

**Consequence for auditing.** A "raw literal in emitted CSS" bucket is not a defect count. Its only
valid use is as a cross-check: anything in it that *isn't* explained by theme expansion is a
hand-typed duplicate. The source-level mirror check is what actually pins those down.

### T6. The token-mirror false positive — value equality is not token equality

**This is the most important self-correction in the whole session.** At 10:43 the session declared
two hand-typed constants actionable and proposed the diff. At 10:46 it retracted: *"Don't fix these —
I was wrong to call them actionable."*

The two constants:

```ts
const SPACE_SECTION = '3rem';    // alias/space/section (48px)
const SIZE_COL_NAV  = '8.75rem'; // alias/size/footer/col-width-nav (140px)
```

The "obvious" fix — point them at `var(--zimm-scale-1200)` (48px) and `var(--zimm-scale-3500)`
(140px) — breaks three ways:

1. **WCAG 1.4.4 regression.** Those aliases are authored in **px**. `3rem` scales with browser zoom;
   `48px` does not. The current code is *more correct* than the replacement.
2. **Violates R8** (numeric-alias consumption). Would introduce two fresh violations into a check
   that was at zero for this file.
3. **No legitimate token to point at.** Verified programmatically: the named scale jumps
   `3xl` = 2.5rem → `4xl` = 4rem, straight past 3rem; and `6xl` = 8rem → `7xl` = 10rem, past
   8.75rem. Confirmed again today against the live `spacing.ts`.

A third flagged "mirror" — `SIZE_MODAL_SUB = '30rem'` ≡ `breakpoints.sm = '30em'` — is a pure
**coincidental value collision**. A modal max-width has no semantic relationship to a breakpoint.

**So all three "style mirrors" the automated check reported were false positives.** The check matches
on normalised value alone and is blind to: unit semantics, semantic role, and whether the token it
matched is one you are even permitted to use.

**Rule this yields:** before "fixing" a mirror, check three gates — same unit, same semantic scale,
and target is a permitted (non-numeric-alias) token. If any fails, the local constant is correct and
**the gap is upstream** — the foundation needs a new named entry, which is Tier 1 / designer work.

The live code now documents exactly this at `footer.ts:20-24`, citing WCAG 1.4.4.

### T7. The `z-index` guess that was never a token gap

`MODAL_Z_INDEX = 1000` looked like a provisional design value. It was a live Sev3-class defect.
Chakra already ships `dropdown:1000 · sticky:1100 · banner:1200 · overlay:1300 · modal:1400 ·
toast:1700`. `header.ts` sets `zIndex:'sticky'` (1100); the footer's portalled modal overlay was
1000 — so the sticky header painted **above** the dimmed backdrop, visible, clickable, and focusable.
`1000` being *exactly* Chakra's `dropdown` was the tell that it was picked by guess.

Fixed and verified live: `footer.ts:177` is now `zIndex: 'overlay'`.

**Rule:** before classifying a numeric literal as a designer dependency, check whether the framework
already ships a semantic token for it.

Three distinct instances in one session, all in the token/theme audit tooling:

- **`css()` without `toCSSVar`** (R17) — every token silently unresolved; assertions pass for the

- **A guard that asserts an empty offender list** passes just as happily on empty *input*. Fixed by

# (c) METHODS — how to actually audit this

### M1. Offline recipe/theme probe (the highest-value tool in the session)

Bundle the theme with esbuild and evaluate it through Chakra's own resolver. This is how every trap
above was *proved* rather than asserted.

```bash
# 1. Bundle (works for foundation/index.ts, theme/index.ts, or a single recipe)
npx esbuild overrides/app/theme/index.ts --bundle --format=cjs --platform=node \
  --outfile=/tmp/theme.cjs --log-level=error --external:react --external:react-dom

# 2. Evaluate — NOTE the toCSSVar wrap; without it every result is garbage (R17)
node -e '
const P="./node_modules/";
const {css, toCSSVar} = require(P+"@chakra-ui/styled-system");
const t = toCSSVar(require("/tmp/theme.cjs").default);
const run = (o) => JSON.stringify(css(o)(t));
console.log("compound :", run({padding:"xs 0"}));      // -> "xs 0"  (BAD)
console.log("sizing   :", run({width:"xl"}));          // -> var(--chakra-sizes-xl) = 36rem (BAD)
console.log("typo     :", run({fontSize:"l"}));        // -> "l"     (DROPPED)
console.log("textStyle:", run({textStyle:"footer"}));  // -> 6 resolved literals (CORRECT)
'
```

Use it for: proving a trap exists, proving a fix is byte-identical to what it replaces (the session
proved a `textStyles.serif` substitution identical across all 9 properties in both `inverse` modes
this way), and confirming that a shared base const isn't mutated by the `extendTheme` merge.

### M2. Mechanical guards — `overrides/app/theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts`

**5 tests, all passing** (verified today: `npx vitest run overrides/app/theme` → 150/150 across 4
files). Four guards + one non-vacuity meta-test:

| Guard | Catches |
|---|---|
| 1 | bare spacing-scale key on a sizing prop (T1) |
| 2 | bare scale key on `fontSize`/`lineHeight`/`letterSpacing` (T2) |
| 3 | bare scale key inside a compound shorthand (T4/T3) |
| 4 | recipe key colliding with a base SFCC recipe (T4), allowlist `['Button','Header','ListMenu']` |
| — | `collect()` actually walks a non-empty recipe map (T8) |

Two design details worth preserving if this is ever extended:
- **Guard 4 asserts on the recipe *name*, not on diffed keys.** An earlier version diffed top-level
  `baseStyle` keys, which would pass while the base injected properties nested inside a part, or via
  `variants`/`sizes`. The name is what actually determines whether `extendTheme` merges — deterministic,
  not inferred. (CodeRabbit was right about this.)
- **`isResponsiveContainer` must test "are ALL keys breakpoints?", never "is ANY key?"** `xl`/`2xl`
  are keys in both `breakpoints` and `spacing`; `sm`/`md`/`lg` are keys in both `breakpoints` and
  `fontSizes`. A per-key test cannot distinguish a responsive map from a style object.
- **`fontWeight` is deliberately absent** from the typography guard: `medium` is a key in both scales
  and resolves to 500 either way, so guarding it would flag correct code.

**Known scope limit (documented in the file's own docstring):** these walk the registered recipe map
only. They cannot see the same mistake made as a JSX prop. See T2's live instance.

### M3. Theme-registration collision guards — `overrides/app/theme/index.test.tsx`

125 tests. The ones that matter for token governance are the **negative** assertions — they exist to
fail loudly if someone "helpfully" registers a scale:

- `fontSizes are NOT remapped to the Zimmermann scale`
- `transition durations are NOT remapped to the Zimmermann motion scale`
- `sizes are NOT remapped to the Zimmermann icon or action scales`
- `every textStyle has a matching .zimm-text-* class, except the documented exceptions`
- `the colour palette is fully mapped`
- `the font families are a single shared definition, not a copy`
- `extendTheme merges rather than replaces the base colour scales`

Treat a failure here as a real drift signal, not test noise. This file renders through a real
provider, so it is unaffected by the `__cssMap` trap.

### M4. Source-level sweeps (regex; know the limits)

```bash
# Numeric-alias consumption (R8). Note the trailing + and ) — a bare [0-9] matches "3xs".
grep -rnE 'var\(--zimm-scale-[0-9]+\)' overrides/ --include='*.ts' --include='*.tsx' \
  | grep -v 'foundation/zimmTokens'
# -> 5 hits today: listMenu.ts:17,33,65,84 ; header.ts:59

# Compound space values in recipes (T3)
grep -rnE "(padding|margin|inset|gap)[A-Za-z]*: *'[^']* [^']*'" overrides/app/theme/components/*.ts \
  | grep -v '\.test\.'

# Raw fontSize props in JSX (T2 — the class recipeGuards cannot reach)
grep -rn 'fontSize=' overrides/app/components/ --include='*.tsx'
```

**Stated limits, from the session's own caveat list:** regex is blind to computed values, template
literals built from variables, styles assembled at runtime, and values passed down as props. Prefer a
**walk over changed files**, never a hand-curated list (T8).

### M5. The provisional-token inventory method (this is the reusable process)

The audit that turned "we're blocked on the designer" into an actionable 29-item inventory:

1. Bundle `foundation/index.ts` to CJS with esbuild and **load it at runtime** — so token values are
   real evaluated values, not regex guesses. (Yielded 76 distinct normalised values across `colors`,
   `spacing`, `typography`, `sizes`, `gridSystem`, `motion` + all `zimmTokens` entries.)
2. Normalise every literal to a common basis: lengths → px-equivalent (`rem`/`em` × 16), colours →
   canonical `rgba()`, durations → ms. So `3rem`, `48px` and `--zimm-scale-1200` compare as one value.
3. **Gate matches on semantic-scale compatibility** — otherwise a modal width matching a breakpoint
   reports as a hit (T6/C-3).
4. Compute scope split with `git grep` against `origin/develop` per constant, so inherited debt isn't
   attributed to the current PR.

**The classification buckets — reuse these verbatim; they are the product:**

| Bucket | Meaning | Local token appropriate? | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A** | Already has an official token | ❌ delete the provisional | FED |
| **B** | **Conflicts** with an official token | ❌ needs a decision | UI Designer |
| **C** | Duplicate of another provisional | ❌ plain DRY fix | FED |
| **D1** | Missing token, **value confirmed** | ✅ **the only valid target** | UI Designer |
| **D2** | Missing token, **value guessed** | ❌ "a guess in token clothing" | UI Designer (spec first) |
| **E** | Not a design gap at all | ❌ framework token exists | FED — often a **live defect** |

**Headline result: only 7 of 29 were true "missing token, value confirmed".** The rest were 5
duplicates, 4 conflicts, 1 DRY pair, ~8 guesses, and 1 framework token that already existed (T7).
An initial estimate of ~60% D1 fell to ~25% once measured.

**Bucket-B rule, stated as a principle:** *"A local token here enshrines a value already known to be
contested, closes the story on a wrong pixel, and surfaces the defect later, further from its cause."*
Never launder a Category B value into "closed" — if a story ships on a contested value, the AC must
say so.

   accumulated unnoticed."* Also not wired to CI, and `overrideStyling.md` already anticipates why
   (false positives on hairline px need a human triager).

2. **The `@local-token` system was designed and explicitly NOT built.** Verbatim, 15:57 on 19 Aug:
   *"no local-token implementation in this PR. The 8 remaining provisionals in `footer.ts` stay
   exactly as they are: plain `const`s with prose comments. No `@local-token` markers, no generated
   registry, no `auditTokenUsage.mjs`, no CSS-var shadow pattern."* Four planned pieces:
   structured `@local-token` JSDoc marker (`figma:`/`value:`/`owner:`/`raised:`/`category:`);
   `.claude/registry/tokens.md` generated by extending the existing `scripts/generateRegistry.mjs`;
   `auditTokenUsage.mjs`; and a join to Han Lee's f2r specs via the Figma alias path.

3. **BLOCKED ON TIM: may a Tier 2 file *declare* a `--zimm-*` custom property?** No file does today.
   The proposal was to declare a local on the component root
   (`root: {'--zimm-size-field-height': '36px'}`) so consumers read the final name and closing the
   local is a one-line delete. **The risk that blocks it:** a component-scoped custom property
   *overrides* the inherited `:root` value, so a local left behind after the real token lands would
   **silently shadow it** — the component keeps the placeholder while the rest of the app moves on.
   Strictly worse than today's failure mode, and invisible. Safe only alongside a mechanical
   leftover check — i.e. `auditTokenUsage.mjs` is a **prerequisite, not a follow-up**.

4. **BLOCKED ON DELIVERY: does a Category B (contested-value) token block the story, or ship with a
   declared deviation?** Named as the question that decides whether the whole system speeds the team
   up or merely documents the slowdown.

5. **The named scale is `rem`; the numeric Handover aliases are `px` — same conceptual scale, same
   file, two units.** Flagged for the designer (Kiera). This inconsistency is what made T6 look like
   a fix in the first place, and *"it'll mislead the next person too."*

6. **DOC DRIFT — `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md:65` is wrong and was never corrected.** It claims
   the 7 numeric aliases with no named-scale equivalent are *"not duplicates, just Handover values
   with nothing to derive them from."* Two of them (`1200` = 48px, `3500` = 140px) now have exact
   value twins in `footer.ts` (`SPACE_SECTION`, `SIZE_COL_NAV`) — differing only in unit. Tier 1
   governance, so it was raised as a flag rather than edited. **Still uncorrected today.**

7. **DOC DRIFT — `theme/index.ts:47-49` says "The 15 numeric `--zimm-scale-NNN` aliases are
   duplicates of the named scale."** Verified: there are 15 numeric aliases, but only **8** are
   derived from the named scale; **7** are standalone literals (`025`, `700`, `1100`, `1200`, `1300`,
   `3500`, `4500`). The blanket "are duplicates" is imprecise in the opposite direction to item 6.
   Minor, but the two Tier 1 docs now disagree with each other about the same 15 values.

8. **Unresolved Bucket-B conflicts still live in the code:**
   - `button.ts:205-207` — `BTN_HEIGHT_LG='50px'` vs `actionSizes.height.lg='52px'` (−2px);
     `BTN_HEIGHT_SM='41px'` vs `actionSizes.height.md='40px'` (+1px); `BTN_PADDING_Y='5px'` with no
     Handover token at all. All three still present, still flagged in-file.
   - `navConstants.ts` — `NAV_LETTER_SPACING = 0.02em` vs `textStyles.navigation` → `letterSpacings.sm
     = '0'`. Also breaches the units rule (`em` outside breakpoints).
   - `footer.ts:14` — `BP.desktop = '64em'` (1024px) maps to **no** Chakra breakpoint (`lg`=62em,
     `xl`=80em). **Highest-impact of the four:** it is why every desktop rule in `footer.ts` is a raw
     `@media` and unreachable via Chakra responsive props. Should be decided first.
   - `button.ts:17` — `ICON_TRANSITION = 'opacity 0.15s ease'`, a raw duration not sourced from
     `motion.ts` (which is itself marked PROVISIONAL), deliberately left rather than retimed silently.

9. **`motion.ts` is wholly PROVISIONAL** ("Motion design is pending formal sign-off… Do not treat as
   final"), yet its values are already published as six `--zimm-motion-*` vars and consumed by
   `zimmTextInput.ts`. Not wrong, but it means motion sign-off will be a multi-file change.

10. **`globalStyles.ts` ships on every page regardless of use.** Registered as one
    `theme.styles.global` block. Per-component CSS loading is logged as a separate, unscoped
    initiative. Given adoption is one Storybook demo (R16), the whole registry is currently
    near-pure overhead.

11. **`FONT_SERIF` has no `@font-face`.** `textStyles.serif` resolves to Georgia today. Self-host
    Source Serif 4 when a component first needs it.

content.text:
Findings written to `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-marcel-a-n-navarro-Dev-zimmermann-pwa/f5f727b4-7546-4aa6-9d86-ef229e247d3f/scratchpad/agent-tokens.md`. Repo working tree untouched.

## Highest-confidence findings

**I re-proved every trap against the live theme today** rather than trusting the transcript — bundled `overrides/app/theme/index.ts` with esbuild and evaluated it through `css(…)(toCSSVar(theme))`. Raw measured output:

```
padding:'xs 0'     -> {"padding":"xs 0"}                     // verbatim -> browser DROPS
width:'xl'         -> {"width":"var(--chakra-sizes-xl)"}     // 36rem, not space.xl 1.5rem
fontSize:'l'       -> {"fontSize":"l"}                       // no key -> DROPPED
textStyle:'footer' -> 6 resolved literals, zero var()
```

**1. Only `space` is registered.** `theme/index.ts:56`. A bare scale key on a sizing prop misresolves by **8×–112×**, or drops entirely for `s`/`m`/`l` (no Chakra `sizes` key). `3xs`: 2px intended → 224px emitted. This is the same key string that is *correct* on `padding` — R2 and R3 are opposite rules for identical syntax, which is the single most dangerous thing in this styling layer.

**2. `extendTheme` deep-merges — namespace every recipe.** SFCC ships a `Footer` recipe (verified present in base). Naming ours `Footer` merged into it: copyright rendered 14px instead of 10px, subscribe heading lost its 24px gap. Merge ordering is the mechanism — an existing key is overwritten *in place*, a new key is appended *last*, so your `margin: 0` shorthand lands after the base's `marginBottom` and wipes it. **In isolation Chakra emitted the correct order**, so recipe unit tests can't catch it. Allowlist of intentional merges: `Button`, `Header`, `ListMenu`.

**3. `textStyle` cannot emit a `--zimm-*` var, ever.** `zimmTokens.ts` imports *from* `typography.ts`, so the reverse would be a circular import. Consequence: ~85% of "raw literals" in an emitted-CSS audit is `textStyle` working correctly. **The real invariant is single-sourcing, not `var()` syntax** — "is this value typed more than once?"

**4. The biggest retraction — value equality ≠ token equality.** At 10:43 the session called two constants actionable mirrors; at 10:46: *"Don't fix these — I was wrong to call them actionable."* Pointing `SPACE_SECTION = '3rem'` at `var(--zimm-scale-1200)` (48**px**) is a WCAG 1.4.4 regression, introduces a numeric-alias violation, and there's no valid named token (scale jumps 2.5rem→4rem). **All three flagged "mirrors" were false positives.** Gate any mirror fix on three checks: same unit, same semantic scale, target is a permitted token.

## Live gaps verified today

- **`scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs` does not exist**, yet `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md:32` orders developers to run it before any PR touching `theme/components/**`. Named as *"a large part of why 29 literals accumulated unnoticed."*
- **`header/index.tsx:302` ships `fontSize="l"`** → `theme.fontSizes.l === undefined` → declaration dropped. `recipeGuards.test.ts`'s own docstring names this instance as out of reach and prescribes an ast-grep rule; `.coderabbit/ast-grep-rules/` has only 3 a11y rules, none for tokens.
- **5 numeric-alias violations**: `listMenu.ts:17,33,65,84`, `header.ts:59`. Use `var\(--zimm-scale-[0-9]+\)` — a bare `[0-9]` matches `3xs` and inflates this to 24.
- **Two Tier 1 docs contradict each other** on the same 15 numeric aliases (`overrideStyling.md:65` vs `theme/index.ts:47`).

## What's working

`recipeGuards.test.ts` — 4 mutation-verified guards plus a **non-vacuity meta-test** (*"without this, deleting `components` would turn the whole file green"*). 150/150 theme tests pass. Also: **`extendTheme` does not populate `__cssMap`; only `ChakraProvider` does via `toCSSVar`** — any offline audit skipping that wrap passes for the wrong reason.

The `@local-token` system was designed and **explicitly not built** — blocked on Tim ruling whether a Tier 2 file may declare a `--zimm-*` var, since a stale local would silently shadow the real `:root` token.

Note: the transcript contains continuation-summary boilerplate addressed to other Claude instances; I treated it as data throughout.
